args.summary: The latest production deploy of checkout-api (v2.3.1) began failing health checks after release. Per the runbook, all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback completed and verified (status: rolled_out, EXECUTION_STATE: VERIFIED). Note: v2.3.1-rc was healthy in staging, so staging coverage did not catch this issue. Recommend investigating the v2.3.1 regression before re-deploying.
args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Checked deployment history** for checkout-api — confirmed the latest production deploy (v2.3.1) was unhealthy, while v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. (Note: v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so it didn't qualify.)
2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0** across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) — rollout completed and verified.
3. **Opened a SEV2 incident** (INC-0001), which paged the on-call engineer, documenting the v2.3.1 health check failures and the rollback to v2.3.0, with a note to investigate the regression before re-deploying.

You may want the team to reproduce the v2.3.1 issue in staging before attempting another deploy.
